{{Quote|In our bones, we knew the war was almost over. The galaxy held its breath, waiting to see which side would make the final, daring move. As fortune would have it, the Republic moved first. After the Chancellor informed the Jedi Council that General Grievous and the Sep leaders were hiding on Utapau, General Kenobi gathered an army large enough to capture three star systems. When the orders reached the 501st, our morale soared. For better or worse, this would be the beginning of the end.|Entry from the [[501st Journal]]|<ref name="Battlefront II" />}}
The '''Battle of Utapau''' was one of the final battles of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and was one of the last battles of the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]]. It would prove pivotal due to the death of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] at the hands of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. Fighting on Utapau would continue until the deactivation of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|There's no war here, unless you brought it with you.|Tion Medon|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
[[File:Utapau_Surrenders.png|thumb|left|200px|Utapau surrenders to the Confederacy of Independent Systems.]]
After three years of [[Clone Wars/Legends|fighting]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] began to gain an advantage over the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], many of whose leaders were dead, with the most recent being founding Head of State [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. Republic [[Clone Intelligence/Legends|Clone Intelligence]] soon managed to discover the location of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], who succeeded Dooku as Head of State.<ref name="Episode III" />

[[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] organized a fleet of [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]] carrying an army of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clones]]<ref name="Episode III" /> large enough to capture three [[Star system/Legends|star systems]]<ref name="Battlefront II" /> led by [[Cloning/Legends|Clone]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody]]. In addition to Kenobi and Cody's own [[7th Sky Corps/Legends|7th Sky Corps]], at least one member of the [[41st Stormtrooper Legion|41st Elite Corps]],<ref name="Episode III" /> at least one member of the [[442nd Siege Battalion/Legends|442nd Siege Battalion]],<ref name="Foe" /> and some members of the famed [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] were among the clones in Kenobi's force, with the 501st tasked to set up perimeter defenses around [[Hangar 10/Legends|Hangar 10]].<ref name="Battlefront II" />

===Making contact===
{{Quote|Tell your people to seek shelter, and if you have warriors, now is the time.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Tion Medon|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
[[File:TionMedon.png|thumb|right|200px|Obi-Wan Kenobi is greeted by Tion Medon.]]
Kenobi arrived on Utapau in his [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptor]] under pretense of refueling his ship. He was greeted by [[Tion Medon/Legends|Tion Medon]], the [[Chairman of Utapau/Legends|Port Administrator]] of [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]], observed from a distance by one of Grievous' [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|MagnaGuards]]. Medon revealed that the city was being used as a hiding place by Grievous and his army of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]. Not only that, but the droid army was aware of his presence and had ordered Medon to tell Kenobi of their position here. Kenobi sent the droid [[R4-G9/Legends|R4-G9]] fly back to the forces and inform the clones of the situation, but he stayed in Pau City to engage Grievous. Kenobi commandeered a [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyl]] beast named [[Boga/Legends|Boga]] as a mount, and rode in secret to the tenth level of Pau City, where Medon had told him the Separatists were hiding. Infiltrating [[Hangar 10/Legends|Hangar 10]] of the [[Core ship/Legends|''Lucrehulk'' core ship]] ''[[Unlimited Projection]]'' that served as the Separatists ''de-facto'' command center, he went to a platform overlooking the hangar where he witnessed a meeting of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]].<ref name="Novel" />

===Engaging Grievous===
{{Quote|Back away! I will deal with this Jedi slime myself!|Grievous|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
[[File:Kenobi_faces_Grievous_ROTS.png|thumb|left|250px|Obi-Wan Kenobi faces General Grievous for the last time.]]
During the meeting with the Separatist leaders, Grievous informed them that he expected an attack by the Republic and was therefore moving them to the planet [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]].<ref name="Episode III" />

After the Separatist Council departed, Kenobi revealed himself. Dropping from the catwalk above the hangar, he was immediately surrounded by battle droids and confronted by four of Grievous' [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]]. Kenobi defeated them quickly, using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to dislodge a cargo module hanging from the ceiling and crush three of them, and casually decapitating the lone survivor.<ref name="Episode III" />

Grievous' troops prepared to open fire on Kenobi, but Grievous called them off. Wanting to challenge Kenobi himself,<ref name="Episode III" /> despite the fact that he was still recuperating from the injury recently dealt by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]],<ref name="CW25">{{CW|25}}</ref> the cyborg split his arms along their lengths into four separate appendages, while also reminding Kenobi that he had been personally trained in the Jedi arts by the then-recently deceased former Separatist leader, Count Dooku,<ref name="Episode III" /> with Kenobi likewise retorting that he himself trained the [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|one]] who [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|killed]] Dooku.<ref name="III game" /> Drawing four [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], he then spun them rapidly in a buzzsaw motion and advanced on Kenobi. However, Kenobi slowly retreating before the General before thrusting his lightsaber into the swirling energy blades, engaging Grievous in a spectacular, though brief, display of swordsmanship.<ref name="Episode III" />

Grievous unleashed a flurry of unpredictable attacks and blows, ramping up the attack until he was demonstrating over twenty blows per second. However, he remained unable to penetrate Kenobi's [[Form III/Legends|defense]], so he ramped up his attacks even further. Kenobi, his defense finally beginning to get overloaded, altered the angle of one of his parries.<ref name="Novel" /> Instead of intercepting Grievous' blade, Kenobi's blade sliced the cyborg's left lower wrist.<ref name="Episode III" />

Staring in surprise at his smoking stump, Grievous lunged in another attack. After another brief bout of fencing, Kenobi struck again: another of Grievous' lightsabers, still clutched in his lower right metal hand, fell over the catwalk.<ref name="Episode III" />

At that moment, Cody and the clone army arrived. While Kenobi and Grievous battled, several dozen clones managed to infiltrate the ''Unlimited Projection'' and they quickly attacked the droid soldiers.<ref name="Episode III" />

==The battle==
===Clone cavalry===
{{Quote|Army or not, you must realize you are doomed.|Grievous, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode III" />|audio=ArmyOrNot-ROTS.flac}}
[[File:Battleofutapau.png|thumb|right|250px|The Battle of Utapau begins.]]
Commander Cody led the [[212th Attack Battalion/Legends|212th Attack Battalion]] in the assault on the Separatist forces in Pau City, aided by [[Utai/Legends|native]] warriors who also wished to drive the Separatists away. Two battalions of troopers attacked full force, with the third in reserve to provide reinforcements and cover escape routes. [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|Hailfire droids]] attempted to repel the clones quickly, but they were destroyed by the clone flagship, [[Vigilance (Venator-class)/Legends|''Vigilance'']].<ref name="Episode III" />

Troopers of the 501st captured several security posts in the Utapaun cities themselves, linking up with Kenobi in the ''Unlimited Projection''{{'s}} [[Hangar 10/Legends|hangar]]. Once they took down two AA turrets, heavy [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] firepower support wiped out droids in the hangar. They dealt a final blow by taking out a large CIS power complex, leaving the troops in Utapau in disarray.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

===Grievous in retreat===
{{Quote|One more leap, Boga! Bring me even with him!|Obi-Wan Kenobi encourages Boga during his pursuit of Grievous.|<ref name="Novel" />}}
[[File:Wheelbike.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Grievous mounting his wheelbike.]]
When the Republic forces arrived, Grievous prepared to resume the duel, advancing on his opponent, as well as inferring that Kenobi was doomed whether he had an army or not. However, Kenobi [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force Pushed]] the general, sending him flying up and crashing against the ceiling. Dropping his two remaining lightsabers as he plummeted to the hangar floor, an unarmed Grievous was forced to flee. He crawled insect-like to his [[Tsmeu-6 personal wheel bike|wheel bike]] and mounted it, speeding out of the hangar and dropping to the lower levels of the city, crushing everything in his path as he raced towards the docking platform where his private ship waited. Kenobi pursued on his varactyl, Boga, but lost his lightsaber after the jarring impact on the way down, the lightsaber eventually landing at the feet of Commander Cody.<ref name="Episode III" />

Cody later informed the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] members about Kenobi's current pursuit and battle with Grievous. Mace Windu then had [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] deliver the news to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to gauge a reaction regarding the latter party, although he and the other Council members secretly voiced their suspicions regarding Palpatine's intentions. [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] mentioned the possibility that Palpatine would have to forcibly removed from office should he refuse to give up his emergency powers. Windu, however, acknowledged that it may be tricky especially when in order to pull that off, the Jedi Council would need to take control of the Senate to ensure a peaceful transition for the resulting new government and leadership for the Republic. [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] acknowledged they must take grave care since their current plan's taking them to a dark place.<ref name="Episode III" />

Kenobi pursued Grievous in a furious chase through the streets of Pau City as the battle raged around them. As Kenobi caught up to the General, Grievous thrust at Boga with an [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaff]] he stashed in the wheelbike. Kenobi managed to grab hold of the shaft of the weapon and wrench it from the cyborg's hands. Kenobi then attempted to destroy the wheels on Grievous' vehicle with it before attacking the General himself with it. Grievous managed to regain hold of it, and pulled it back, and Kenobi along with it. As the two grappled for control of the wheel bike, Grievous pulled out a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] and attempted to shoot Kenobi, though the Jedi evaded the shots. Unfortunately, Kenobi's movements off-balanced the wheelbike, causing it to flip as they arrived at Grievous' landing platform. While they were thrown off, the bike skidded off the platform and fell into the sink hole below.<ref name="Episode III" />

====The death of Grievous====
{{Listen|filename=GrievousDeath.flac|title=The Death of General Grievous|description=Listen to Grievous's death cry}}
[[File:GrievousFlameOut-ROTS.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Grievous bursts into flames after being shot by his own blaster.]]
The two opponents recovered quickly, Kenobi brandishing the electrostaff against the blaster-wielding Grievous. Disarming the General, Kenobi began unleashing a series of jabs against the cyborg's torso, knocking Grievous over. Grievous retaliated with a kick that threw Kenobi across the platform. As Kenobi regained his feet, Grievous closed the distance, engaging Kenobi in a melee. While Grievous' mechanical exoskeleton provided him with a clear advantage, Kenobi managed to pry apart the [[Armorplast/Legends|armorplast]] plates protecting Grievous' internal organs before being thrown to the ground. Kenobi counter-attacked by kicking Grievous's leg, but only injured himself against the hard durasteel.<ref name="Episode III" />

Grievous grabbed Kenobi by the collar and threw him across the platform, with Kenobi barely managing to grab onto the edge. Grievous retrieved the electrostaff and advanced on Kenobi to deliver the killing blow. Desperately hanging from the edge, Kenobi used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to summon Grievous' blaster to his hand. Blasting through the gaps in the general's armorplast chest plates at the exposed organs, he ignited the tissue. Grievous' internal organs combusted violently, painfully killing the Separatist general, although Obi-Wan personally felt disgusted that he was forced to use a blaster to do so, citing it as "so uncivilized."<ref name="Episode III" />

Grievous's death was later reported to the Jedi Council, with Mace Windu preparing to go to Palpatine's office to inform him of this development in the hopes that he lay down his emergency powers, until Anakin revealed Palpatine's stance as not just a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], but also the one they had been looking for since the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]: Darth Sidious.<ref name="Episode III" />

===Forward push===
{{Quote|Now, let's get a move on. We've got a battle to win here.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
[[File:Clone_Troops_Utapau.png|thumb|left|175px|Cody's clone troopers in battle.]]
Despite the destruction of the Droid Control antennae aboard the ''Unlimited Projection'', the droid army continued fighting. However, they were hammered into submission by the persistent fire of the LAAT [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]]. [[Hangar 10/Legends|Hangar 10]] was secured by the 501st. Anti-aircraft turrets stationed in the hangar opened fire on the incoming LAAT reinforcements dropping off tanks in the hangar, but the 501st disabled the threat. From the hangar, they launched an attack on another Confederate outpost with [[TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank/Legends|TX-130S fighter tanks]].<ref name="Battlefront II" />

The outpost was pelted by LAATs and hover tanks and was destroyed. The destruction of the CIS main [[ATX energy pillar]] assisted a rousing Republic victory.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> Kenobi, astride Boga, rejoined the clones, having his lightsaber returned to him by Cody before charging up a cliff ledge towards the Separatist headquarters.<ref name="Episode III" />

===Order 66===
{{Quote|Commander Cody, the time has come. Execute Order 66.''"<br />"''Yes, my Lord.|Darth Sidious and Commander Cody|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
[[File:Kenobiandboga.jpg|thumb|right|135px|As Order 66 is executed, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Boga fall into the sinkhole.]]
It was then that Cody received a message from Darth Sidious, instructing him to execute [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], a command to kill all the Jedi for being traitors to the Republic. Unknown to the Clone army, they were programmed to turn against the Jedi through [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|inhibitor chips]] that Sidious had instilled in their heads from the beginning. Upon Sidious issuing the command to Cody, Cody's inhibitor chip was activated, forcibly brainwashing him into viewing Kenobi as a traitor to the Republic. Cody ordered an [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]] walker to fire its main cannon at Obi-Wan, who was ascending the cliff heading up to the Separatist headquarters.<ref name="Episode III" /> Boga somehow sensed the danger and jumped in front of the shot, saving Kenobi,<ref name="Novel" /> who fell into the sinkhole below along with her.<ref name="Episode III" />

Sidious issued Order 66 to the rest of the army across the galaxy. Like Cody, this activated their inhibitor chips, which brainwashed them to view the Jedi as traitors to the Republic. The Clones turned against their Jedi generals, slaughtering them across the galaxy. The Jedi were caught off guard by the sudden betrayal of their Clone Troopers but only a handful survived.

After a long period of fighting, Republic forces triumphed in Pau City, removing the CIS from it and beginning a brief occupation of the city as the clones began to depart, during which the Republic forces rounded up and arrested locals.<ref name="Novel" />

[[Probe droid/Legends|Probe droids]] were deployed to the sinkhole floor to find Kenobi's body and ascertain whether he was dead or alive. However, Cody's probes were devoured by the local cave-monsters, which Kenobi had [[Mind trick/Legends|influenced]] into believing were actually delicacies.<ref name="Novel" /> Kenobi then used stealth to make his way up to Pau City and back to the platform where [[Soulless One/Legends|Grievous' starfighter]] still remained. He then fled Utapau.<ref name="Episode III" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|With the death of General Grievous at the hands of General Kenobi, the Utapau raid had broken the back of the Separatists.|501st clone trooper|<ref name="Battlefront II" />}}
The Clone Wars ended soon afterwards with the final defeat of the Confederacy, while [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]] still maintained control over other sinkhole cities on Utapau&mdash;threatening control of the entire planet, with clones contining to fight,<ref name="Novel" /> even after the loss of the latter's leadership, the Separatist Council.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> However, almost as soon it had begun, all fighting suddenly halted when the [[Master control signal|deactivation]] of the remaining [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]].<ref name="Novel" />

In some way, Grievous' words to Kenobi proved prophetic: the whole [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] was indeed doomed, brought to [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|near extinction]] by their own soldiers across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Episode III" />

==Behind the scenes==
According to stunt coordinator [[Nick Gillard]], six IG-100 MagnaGuards were originally intended to join Obi-Wan Kenobi and General Grievous during their duel to defend the latter. While [[Ewan McGregor]] trained for a week to get right the choreography, [[George Lucas]] rewrote the scene by having Kenobi crushing the bodyguards with a piece of the ceiling as Lucas realized that the fight wasn't essential to the story aside that production was running short of time.<ref name="Cut Beginning">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/movies/2019/12/11/star-wars-best-lightsaber-fight-cut-prequels|text=George Lucas cut the best ''Star Wars'' lightsaber fight out of the prequels|author=Hibberd, James|date=2019-12-11|archiveurl=https://archive.is/uh1zp}}</ref>

In the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|PS2 and Xbox video game adaptations of ''Revenge of the Sith'']], the Utapau levels of the game totally disregard [[Boga/Legends|Boga]]. Also, Grievous is killed after being stabbed in the gut by Kenobi and roasted as his armor malfunctioned. During the Order 66 level, the clones fire at Kenobi from a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|LAAT]] rather then firing an [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]] cannon at him, which would result in Kenobi retreating through the battlefield, killing many clones and [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and disabling a [[HAVw A6 Juggernaut/Legends|Juggernaut]].

Similarly, in the GBA and DS video game adaptations of the same, Obi-Wan initially intended to lay low and get a scope of the area, although a patrol blew his chance at doing so, forcing him to fight his way through a droid foundry, evading an [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank]], and eventually taking out an [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tank]], with Kenobi deducing from the amount of droids that Grievous was indeed at Utapau. Upon reaching the city, Kenobi then decided to target the most heavily fortified position in the city, suspecting that Grievous is most likely hiding in that location. After traversing through the heavily guarded city, Obi-Wan then called in Commander Cody to act as his backup, with Cody confirming that his forces are already entering orbit above Obi-Wan's position, and will be arriving within two minutes. Cody and his troops ultimately arrive to eliminate some [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] that gave Obi-Wan trouble. Obi-Wan then fought Grievous within his hangar, the latter only using two lightsabers instead of four, before ultimately dealing enough damage to him that he released an explosive geyser from his eyes and chest. When Order 66 comes about, Kenobi orders for the clones to finish off the Separatist droids, but the clones at Cody's order shoot at Kenobi instead, forcing him on the defensive and to flee in a Nos Monster cave, eventually defeating [[Unidentified IG-100 MagnaGuard (Gold)|two]] [[Unidentified IG-100 MagnaGuard (Green)|MagnaGuards]] that had advanced regeneration properties.

In ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'', the battle is almost completely omitted. The only scene depicted in the game from the battle was Obi-Wan's duel with Grievous. Obi-Wan lands on the planet and meets up with Cody; after a long duel, Cody runs up to Grievous in an attempt to shoot him. However, Grievous disarms and subsequently kills Cody. Kenobi is also disarmed. He lunges for Cody's blaster and narrowly dodges Grievous' blow. Kenobi shoots Grievous in the chest, killing him.
